title_ja: 中国製木製モールディング・建具部材の反ダンピング審査最終結果
original_text:
[Page 1]
This document is scheduled to be published in the
                                   Federal Register on 2026-11-13 and available online at
                                                                                 BILLING CODE: 3510-DS-P
                                   https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-23084, and on

DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE

International Trade Administration

[A-570-117]

Wood Mouldings and Millwork Products from the People’s Republic of China: Final

Results of Antidumping Duty Administrative Review; 2024-2025

AGENCY: Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, Department of

             Commerce.

SUMMARY: The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) determines that Fujian Hongjia

Craft Products Co., Ltd. (Hongjia), and Nanping Huatai Wood & Bamboo Co., Ltd. (Nanping

Huatai), exporters of wood mouldings and millwork products (millwork products) from the

People’s Republic of China (China), sold subject merchandise in the United States at prices

below normal value during the period of review (POR) February 01, 2024, through January 31,

2025.

DATES: Applicable [INSERT DATE OF PUBLICATION IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER].

[Contact block omitted.]
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

Background

        On May 13, 2026, Commerce published in the Federal Register the Preliminary Results

of this administrative review and invited parties to comment.1 On August 13, 2026, Commerce




1 See Wood Mouldings and Millwork Products from the People’s Republic of China:   Preliminary Results and
Rescission, in Part, of Antidumping Duty Administrative Review; 2024-2025, 91 FR 26999 (May 13, 2026)
(Preliminary Results), and accompanying Preliminary Decision Memorandum (PDM).

[Page 2]
extended the deadline for these final results by 53 days.2 On November 2, 2026, Commerce

extended the deadline for these final results by an additional seven days.3 The deadline for these

final results is November 9, 2026.

        For details of events subsequent to the Preliminary Results, see the Issues and Decision

Memorandum.4 The Issues and Decision Memorandum is a public document and is on file

electronically via Enforcement and Compliance’s Antidumping and Countervailing Duty

Centralized Electronic Service System (ACCESS). ACCESS is available to registered users at

https://access.trade.gov. In addition, a complete version of the Issues and Decision

Memorandum can be accessed directly at https://access.trade.gov/frnotices.

Scope of the Order5

        The products covered by the Order are millwork products from China. For a complete

description of the scope of the Order, see the Issues and Decision Memorandum.

Verification

        As provided in section 782(i) of the Act, in the Preliminary Results Commerce informed

interested parties that it intended to verify the information relied upon in the final results of

review. Accordingly, Commerce notified the mandatory respondents in this review of the dates

and locations where Commerce intended to conduct verification of the information submitted by

the mandatory respondents.6 However, Commerce was unable to conduct verification because

both mandatory respondents withdrew their participation from verification.7

Analysis of Comments Received


2 See Memorandum, “Extension of Deadline for Final Results of Antidumping Duty Administrative Review,” dated

August 13, 2026.
3 See Memorandum, “Extension of Deadline for Final Results of Antidumping Duty Administrative Review,” dated

November 2, 2026.
4 See Memorandum, “Issues and Decision Memorandum for the Final Results of the Antidumping Duty

Administrative Review of Wood Mouldings and Millwork Products from the People’s Republic of China; 2024-
2025,” dated concurrently with, and hereby adopted by, this notice (Issues and Decision Memorandum).
5 See Wood Mouldings and Millwork Products from the People’s Republic of China: Amended Final Antidumping

Duty Determination and Antidumping Duty Order, 86 FR 9486 (February 16, 2021) (Order).
6 See Memorandum, “Verification Schedule,” dated May 21, 2026 (Verification Schedule).
7 See Hongjia’s Letter, “Notification of Action,” dated June 26, 2026 (Hongjia’s Withdrawal of Participation); see

also Nanping Huatai’s Letter, “Notification of Action,” dated June 26, 2026 (Nanping Huatai’s Withdrawal of
Participation).

[Page 3]
All issues raised by interested parties in case and rebuttal briefs are addressed in the

Issues and Decision Memorandum. For a list of the issues addressed in the Issues and Decision

Memorandum, see Appendix I to this notice.

Changes Since the Preliminary Results

       Based on review of the record and comments received from interested parties, we made

changes to the Preliminary Results. Because Hongjia and Nanping Huatai refused to allow

verification of their information submitted in this segment of the proceeding, we determine that

Hongjia’s and Nanping Huatai’s data could not be verified pursuant to section 776(a)(2)(D) of

the Act. Further, due to Hongjia’s and Nanping Huatai’s failure to cooperate by not acting to the

best of their ability to comply with a request for information, we find that the application of facts

available with an adverse inference (AFA) is warranted, pursuant to sections 776(a) and

776(b)(1)(A) of the Act. Accordingly, as Commerce determines that Hongjia’s and Nanping

Huatai’s responses in this proceeding are unverifiable, and the application of AFA is appropriate,

we conclude that the respondents did not demonstrate eligibility for a separate rate in this review

and, thus, are considered part of the China-wide entity for these final results. For further details

on the changes since the Preliminary Results, see the Issues and Decision Memorandum.

       In the Preliminary Results, Commerce also assigned a weighted-average of the

mandatory respondents’ rates to the non-selected separate rate companies. For these final

results, because the information provided by the mandatory companies has not been verified and

we are applying AFA, we are assigning a separate rate calculated in the most recently completed

review of the Order. See the Issues and Decision Memorandum for further discussion.

Separate Rates

       In the Preliminary Results, we preliminarily granted a separate rate to both mandatory

respondents. However, because we were unable to verify information submitted by the two

mandatory respondents, Hongjia and Nanping Huatai, regarding their eligibility for a separate

[Page 4]
rate, we find this information unreliable. Therefore, we determine that Hongjia and Nanping

Huatai are not eligible for a separate rate and find them to be part of the China-Wide entity.

        For the companies eligible for a separate rate in this review, we relied on the weighted-

average dumping margin calculated for non-examined separate rate companies in the previous

administrative review of the Order (i.e., 37.24 percent ad valorem).8 See the Issues and Decision

Memorandum for further discussion.

        In the Preliminary Results, Commerce granted separate rate status to Bel Trade Wood

Industrial Co., Ltd. Youxi Fujian and Tim Feng Manufacturing Co., Ltd. No parties commented

on Commerce’s preliminary separate rate determinations for these companies, and they are

unchanged in these final results of review.

China-Wide Entity

        Commerce’s policy regarding conditional review of the China-wide entity applies to this

administrative review.9 Under this policy, the China-wide entity will not be under review unless

a party specifically requests, or Commerce self-initiates, a review of the entity. Because no party

requested a review of the China-wide entity, the entity is not under review and the dumping

margin assigned to the China-wide entity, i.e., 220.87 percent,10 is not subject to change as a

result of this administrative review.

        Commerce preliminarily found Putian Yihong Wood Industry Co., Ltd. (Putian Yihong)

is not eligible for a separate rate.11 On May 29, 2026, Commerce placed on the record entry

documents pertaining to Putian Yihong.12 No parties commented on the Putian Yihong Entry




8 See Wood Mouldings and Millwork Products from the People’s Republic of China: Final Results of Antidumping
Duty Administrative Review; 2023– 2024, 91 FR 8823 (February 24, 2026) (Millwork Products AR3).
9 See Antidumping Proceedings: Announcement of Change in Department Practice for Respondent Selection in

Antidumping Duty Proceedings and Conditional Review of the Nonmarket Economy Entity in NME Antidumping
Duty Proceedings, 78 FR 65963 (November 4, 2013).
10 See Order, 86 FR at 9488.
11 See Preliminary Results at Appendix V and accompanying PDM at 11.
12 See Memorandum, “Placing U.S. Customs and Border Protection Entry Documents on the Record,” dated May

29, 2026 (Putian Yihong Entry Documents Memorandum).

[Page 5]
Documents Memorandum. Therefore, we continue to find that Putian Yihong is not eligible for

a separate rate, and is part of China-wide entity.13

Final Results of Administrative Review

         For the companies subject to this review that are eligible for a separate rate, Commerce

determines that the following estimated weighted-average dumping margins exist for the period

February 1, 2024, through January 31, 2025:

                                                       Weighted-Average Dumping Margin
                        Exporter
                                                                   (percent)
 Bel Trade Wood Industrial Co., Ltd. Youxi                           37.24
 Fujian Tim Feng Manufacturing Co., Ltd.                             37.24

Disclosure

         Normally, Commerce discloses to interested parties the calculations performed in

connection with the final results of review within five days of any public announcement or, if

there is no public announcement, within five days of the date of publication of the notice of final

results in the Federal Register, in accordance with 19 CFR 351.224(b). However, because we

determine that Hongjia and Nanping Huatai to be part of the China-Wide entity and subject to

the China-wide entity rate which is not subject to change, there are no calculations to disclose.

Assessment Rates

         Pursuant to section 751(a)(2)(C) of the Act and 19 CFR 351.212(b)(1), Commerce has

determined, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) shall assess, antidumping duties on

all appropriate entries of subject merchandise in accordance with the final results of this review.

For the companies listed above, which have been assigned a weighted-average dumping margin

that is not zero or de minimis (i.e., less than 0.5 percent), Commerce will instruct CBP to assess

antidumping duties on all appropriate entries of subject merchandise at a rate equal to the

weighted-average dumping margin assigned to the companies. The companies eligible for a

separate rate have been assigned a rate of 37.24 percent, which is the non-selected separate rate



13 See Appendix II to this notice.

[Page 6]
from Millworks AR3.14 Additionally, we will instruct CBP to apply the China-wide entity rate of

220.87 percent to all POR entries of subject merchandise exported by the China-wide entity.

        Commerce intends to issue assessment instructions to CBP no earlier than 35 days after

the date of publication in the Federal Register of these final results. If a timely summons is filed

at the U.S. Court of International Trade, the assessment instructions will direct CBP not to

liquidate relevant entries until the time for parties to file a request for a statutory injunction has

expired (i.e., within 90 days of publication).

Cash Deposit Requirements

        The following cash deposit requirements will be effective upon publication of these final

results for all shipments of the subject merchandise from China entered, or withdrawn from

warehouse, for consumption on or after the publication date of these final results, as provided by

section 751(a)(2)(C) of the Act: (1) for the companies eligible for a separate rate identified in

the table above, the cash deposit rate will be equal to the weighted-average dumping margin

listed in the table above; (2) for all Chinese exporters of subject merchandise that have not been

found to be entitled to a separate rate, the cash deposit rate will be the rate for the China-wide

entity (i.e., 220.87 percent); and (3) for all non-Chinese exporters of subject merchandise which

have not received their own separate rate, the cash deposit rate will be the rate applicable to the

Chinese exporter that supplied that non-Chinese exporter. These cash deposit requirements,

when imposed, shall remain in effect until further notice.

Notification to Importers Regarding the Reimbursement of Duties

        This notice also serves as a final reminder to importers of their responsibility under 19

CFR 351.402(f)(2) to file a certificate regarding the reimbursement of antidumping and/or

countervailing duties prior to liquidation of the relevant entries during this POR. Failure to

comply with this requirement could result in Commerce’s presumption that reimbursement of

antidumping and/or countervailing duties has occurred and the subsequent assessment of double


14 See Millwork Products AR3, 91 FR at 8824.

[Page 7]
antidumping duties and/or an increase in the amount of antidumping duties by the amount of the

countervailing duties.

Administrative Protective Order (APO)

       This notice also serves as a reminder to parties subject to an APO of their responsibility

concerning the return or destruction of proprietary information disclosed under APO in

accordance with 19 CFR 351.305(a)(3), which continues to govern business proprietary

information in this segment of the proceeding. Timely written notification of the return or

destruction of APO materials, or conversion to judicial protective order, is hereby requested.

Failure to comply with the regulations and terms of an APO is a violation which is subject to

sanction.

Notification to Interested Parties

       We are issuing and publishing these final results of administrative review and notice in

accordance with sections 751(a)(1) and 777(i) of the Act.

Dated: November 6, 2026.
[Signer name omitted.]
Executive Director
 for Policy and Negotiations.

[Page 8]
Appendix I

            List of Topics Discussed in the Issues and Decision Memorandum

I.     Summary
II.    Background
III.   Scope of the Order
IV.    Changes Since the Preliminary Results
V.     Discussion of the Issues
       Comment 1: Whether to Apply Adverse Facts Available to the Mandatory Respondents
       Comment 2: Whether to Use the Expected Method in Assigning a Separate Rate to the
                      Non-Selected Respondents
       Comment 3: Whether the Excessive Fines Clause of the Eighth Amendment Applies to
                      Commerce’s Facts Available Provisions
VI.    Recommendation

[Page 9]
Appendix II

                 Companies Considered to Be Part of the China-Wide Entity

   1. Fujian Hongjia Craft Products Co., Ltd.
   2. Fujian Jinquan Trade Co., Ltd.
   3. Fujian Wangbin Decorative Material Co., Ltd.
   4. Fujian Yinfeng Imp & Exp Trading Co., Ltd/Fujian Province Youxi City Mangrove
      Wood Machining Co., Ltd.
   5. Nanping Huatai Wood & Bamboo Co., Ltd.
   6. Putian Yihong Wood Industry Co., Ltd.
   7. Shenzhen Xinjintai Industrial Co., Ltd.

translation_ja:
## 4ページ（対象箇所）

提出資料が信頼できないと判断し、Fujian HongjiaとNanping Huataiは独立税率の要件を満たさず、中国全体主体に属すると認定した。独立税率対象企業には前回審査の非個別審査企業の加重平均37.24％を用いる。Bel TradeとFujian Tim Fengへの独立税率について異議はなく、最終結果で維持する。中国全体主体は今回の審査対象にならず、220.87％は変更されない。

## 5ページ（対象箇所）

Putian Yihongは独立税率の要件を満たさず、中国全体主体に属すると引き続き判断する。2024年2月1日～2025年1月31日の加重平均マージン。

| 輸出者 | マージン |
|---|---:|
| Bel Trade Wood Industrial Co., Ltd. Youxi | 37.24％ |
| Fujian Tim Feng Manufacturing Co., Ltd. | 37.24％ |

HongjiaとNanping Huataiの中国全体率は変更対象外のため、開示する計算はない。

## 6ページ（対象箇所）

中国全体主体が輸出した審査対象の輸入申告には220.87％を適用するようCBPに指示する。商務省は最終結果の官報掲載後35日より前に賦課指示を出さない方針。掲載後の輸入申告または保税倉庫からの引き出しに対する現金供託は、独立税率が認められた表の企業には表の率、その他の該当中国輸出者には220.87％、独自の率を持たない中国以外の輸出者には供給した中国輸出者の適用率。供託条件は別途通知まで継続する。
facts_ja: 中国製木製モールディング・建具部材の審査最終表でBel Trade Wood Industrial YouxiとFujian Tim Feng各37.24％。中国全体率220.87％は従来値。
企業別の調達負担の変化は今後の供託指示と輸入内訳で確認。
inference_ja: 建材輸入費への影響は対象品と輸出者構成、代替供給、在庫に依存。

results for all shipments of the subject merchandise from China entered, or withdrawn from

warehouse, for consumption on or after the publication date of these final results, as provided by

section 751(a)(2)(C) of the Act: (1) for the companies eligible for a separate rate identified in

the table above, the cash deposit rate will be equal to the weighted-average dumping margin

listed in the table above; (2) for all Chinese exporters of subject merchandise that have not been

found to be entitled to a separate rate, the cash deposit rate will be the rate for the China-wide

entity (i.e., 220.87 percent); and (3) for all non-Chinese exporters of subject merchandise which

have not received their own separate rate, the cash deposit rate will be the rate applicable to the

Chinese exporter that supplied that non-Chinese exporter. These cash deposit requirements,

when imposed, shall remain in effect until further notice.

Notification to Importers Regarding the Reimbursement of Duties

        This notice also serves as a final reminder to importers of their responsibility under 19

CFR 351.402(f)(2) to file a certificate regarding the reimbursement of antidumping and/or

countervailing duties prior to liquidation of the relevant entries during this POR. Failure to

comply with this requirement could result in Commerce’s presumption that reimbursement of

antidumping and/or countervailing duties has occurred and the subsequent assessment of double

Administrative Protective Order (APO)

       This notice also serves as a reminder to parties subject to an APO of their responsibility

concerning the return or destruction of proprietary information disclosed under APO in

accordance with 19 CFR 351.305(a)(3), which continues to govern business proprietary

information in this segment of the proceeding. Timely written notification of the return or

destruction of APO materials, or conversion to judicial protective order, is hereby requested.

Failure to comply with the regulations and terms of an APO is a violation which is subject to

sanction.

       We are issuing and publishing these final results of administrative review and notice in

accordance with sections 751(a)(1) and 777(i) of the Act.
